_meta.indication: RECARBRIO is indicated in patients 18 years of age and older who have limited or no alternative treatment options for complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI), including pyelonephritis, and complicated intra-abdominal infections (cIAI) caused by susceptible gram-negative microorganisms.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, double-blind, randomized, active-controlled, dose-ranging trial in patients with cUTI; randomized 1:1:1 to IMI/REL 250 mg, IMI/REL 125 mg, or IMI/placebo q6h (imipenem 500 mg in all arms).
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with a cUTI or acute pyelonephritis judged by the investigator to be serious (requiring hospitalization and IV antibacterial therapy).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Applicant's primary efficacy endpoint was microbiological response at the discontinuation of IV treatment (DCIV) visit.
pivotal_trials.result: In the MITT population, favorable microbiological response at DCIV was 87.8% for IMI/REL 250 mg vs 92.6% for IMI/placebo (difference -4.8; 95% CI -15.1, 4.9); the trial was not designed or powered for a non-inferiority assessment.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, double-blind, randomized, active-controlled, dose-ranging trial in patients with cIAI; IMI/REL 250 mg, IMI/REL 125 mg, or IMI/placebo q6h IV (imipenem 500 mg in all arms), IV only with no oral switch.
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects with cIAI that required hospitalization and treatment with IV antibacterial therapy.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Applicant's primary analysis was clinical response at the DCIV visit.
pivotal_trials.result: In the MITT population, favorable clinical response at DCIV was 89.9% for IMI/REL 250 mg vs 90.2% for IMI/placebo (difference -0.3; 95% CI -9.6, 8.9); favorable global response rates were similar across arms.

key_safety: The most frequently reported adverse reactions occurring in >=2% of patients treated with imipenem/cilastatin plus relebactam 250 mg were diarrhea, nausea, headache, vomiting, ALT increased, AST increased, phlebitis/infusion site reactions, pyrexia, and hypertension. Serious warnings include hypersensitivity reactions, seizures and other CNS adverse reactions, and Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhea.
target_moa: RECARBRIO combines imipenem (a penem antibacterial whose activity results from binding to PBP 2 and PBP 1B, disrupting bacterial cell wall synthesis), cilastatin (a renal dehydropeptidase inhibitor that limits renal metabolism of imipenem and has no antibacterial activity), and relebactam (a beta-lactamase inhibitor that protects imipenem from degradation by certain serine beta-lactamases such as SHV, TEM, CTX-M, P99, PDC, and KPC).
modality: Small molecule (fixed-dose combination of imipenem, cilastatin, and relebactam for injection).

advisory_committee.vote: An advisory committee meeting was not held for this NDA as there were no specific issues that required expert input.

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for the use of RECARBRIO for the treatment of Hospital-acquired Bacterial Pneumonia/Ventilator-associated Bacterial Pneumonia (HABP/VABP) in adults due to the designated susceptible bacteria.

description.text: Added pediatric patients (birth to <18 years, weighing at least 2 kg) to the approved indications for cUTI, cIAI, and HABP/VABP

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sNDA provides for the addition of pediatric patients (birth to <18 years of age) weighing at least 2 kg to the approved indications for treatment of complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI), including pyelonephritis in patients who have limited or no alternative treatment options; complicated intra-abdominal infections (cIAI) in patients who have limited or no alternative treatment options; and hospital-acquired bacterial pneumonia and ventilator-associated bacterial pneumonia (HABP/VABP).

summary.text: RECARBRIO's relebactam component received Fast Track and QIDP designation on September 13, 2013; the NDA was submitted with Priority review and approved on a standard (non-accelerated) basis, with effectiveness supported in part by FDA's prior findings of efficacy of imipenem plus limited clinical data from trials PN003, PN004, and PN013.
